newsitem.title: USA: US Plains fed cattle market at standstill-feedlots.
newsitem.headline: US Plains fed cattle market at standstill-feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets Friday were at a standstill, with no slaughter steer or heifer sales reported following this week's active sales, feedlot sources said.
The bulk of cattle on this week's showlists sold at $64.00 per cwt, down $1.00 from last week, they said.

However, a few cattle will be carried over to next week after some owners resisted lower packer bids, sources said. Those not sold reportedly were underfinished and could use more days on feed, they said.
Packers lowered bids this week in the face of continued weak beef prices which squeezed operating margins, sources said.
At midday, choice lighter-weight beef was quoted up $0.45 per cwt at $97.32, USDA said. However, that price was down $2.85 from last Friday's close, USDA statistics showed.
Packers reportedly had sufficient inventory to get them into the middle of next week, they said.
Fed cattle prices next week were expected steady but could be firm on ideas packers continued to run "close to the knife" and were short-bought on supplies, one source noted.
